The nanowires were grown by molecular beam epitaxy using a two-stage process, with (In,Ga)As cores grown at 500°C and (Ga,Mn)As shells deposited at 220°C.
The (In,Ga)As cores contain around 10% indium, while the (Ga,Mn)As shells contain approximately 5% manganese.
The nanowires have a diameter of 70-100 nm and a length of up to 1.6 micrometers.
The nanowires exhibit a high-quality wurtzite crystal structure with low defect density, with less than 15% of the nanowires containing structural defects such as basal stacking faults.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells show ferromagnetic coupling at temperatures above 33 K, but the overall magnetic behavior is superparamagnetic.
The Raman scattering data suggests a hole concentration of around 3x10^19 cm^-3 in the (Ga,Mn)As shells, indicating the material is close to the metal-insulator transition.
The (In,Ga)As cores and (Ga,Mn)As shells both have a wurtzite crystal structure, which is different from the cubic zinc-blende structure typically observed in 2D thin films of these materials.
The growth rate of the nanowires is almost 5 times faster than that of the corresponding 2D thin films grown with the same III and V element fluxes.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells are deposited epitaxially on the (In,Ga)As cores without any misfit dislocations at the interface.

The magnetic characterization of the nanowires was challenging due to the need to separate their magnetic signal from that of the substrate, the metallic glue used to anchor the sample, and the (Ga,Mn)As film grown between the nanowires.
The density of the nanowires on the substrate is high, around 2 x 10^9 nanowires/cm^2.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells have a growth rate of about 20 nm/h, which is much lower than the planar growth rate of 200 nm/h for (Ga,Mn)As layers.
The (In,Ga)As layer deposited between the nanowires has a thickness of 300-400 nm.
The (Ga,Mn)As layer deposited between the nanowires has a thickness of up to 70 nm, depending on the shadowing effect due to the inhomogeneous distribution of the nanowires.
The presence of the (Ga,Mn)As film grown between the nanowires complicates the magnetic characterization of the samples.
